summary: Added Textarea, the multi-line field, from the approved 'Component --- Text Area' sheet. It is a separate component rather than a prop on Input because the two differ on the keyboard (Enter submits an Input and inserts a newline here) and on how height is expressed (rows, not a size step) -- one component would have to branch on both. What it DOES share is the control surface: rounded-md, border-[1.5px] border-edge-subtle, bg-field, px-md py-sm, text-body-md, the focus-within border+ring with its forced-colors outline fallback, and the derived hover/invalid/disabled states, all identical to Input's lg. That claim is asserted as a RELATIONSHIP in the browser test -- it mounts a real Input beside the Textarea and compares computed radius, border width, border colour, fill and inset -- rather than as numbers, which would pass while the two silently drifted apart. One divergence, deliberate and documented in the doc's forwarding block: the inset padding sits on the <textarea> rather than on the control wrapper. The native resize grip is painted at the textarea's own corner and the drag sets an inline height on the textarea, so padding on the wrapper would float the grip 12px inside the box and the wrapper would clip the drag instead of growing with it; the inset a user sees is identical, and clicking it now lands on the field rather than on dead wrapper padding. Height is the native rows attribute, defaulted to 6, which is the sheet's 128px box: 6 line boxes over py-sm and the 1.5px border. isResizable (default true) is vertical-only -- a field draggable wider breaks the layout containing it -- and is withdrawn along with the field when isDisabled, so the grip is not the one part of a disabled control that still responds. Label, helperText, errorText, isRequired, isInvalid and the aria-invalid/aria-describedby wiring are Input's contract unchanged, error announced before helper.

migration.manual: Nothing to migrate -- this is a new item. A multi-line field previously had to be hand-rolled or an Input stretched with className, both of which lost the label/error wiring; replace those with <Textarea label="..." rows={n} />. Note there is no size prop: the sheet draws one size, matching Input's lg, and a smaller textarea is recorded under needsDesign rather than invented.
